6GSTARLAB.purpose: 6GStarLab is a 6U CubeSat flown by the Catalan research centre i2CAT as an open in-orbit laboratory for non-terrestrial-network research: rather than delivering a service it lets researchers upload and run their own communications experiments remotely. It carries two Minerva software-defined-radio payloads with multi-band front ends covering UHF/LoRa, S, X and Ka, plus a laser terminal and matching optical and Ka-band ground stations, and exists to validate and help standardise advanced 5G and 6G techniques in a real space channel.

A-SEANSAT-PG1.purpose: A 6U CubeSat developed by the Malaysian company Angkasa-X whose primary mission is tracking seafaring vessels beyond coastal waters across South East Asia using an Automatic Identification System receiver, with a secondary optical imager at up to 5 m ground sample distance. The stated applications include activity and disaster monitoring and search and rescue. Space-based AIS is the cheapest form of wide-area maritime domain awareness, and this is the region's own attempt at it rather than a bought foreign service.

AAC AIS-SAT.purpose: AAC Clyde Space's AIS nanosatellites, 3U EPIC spacecraft built, owned and operated in Glasgow under the company's Space Data as a Service model, which delivers Automatic Identification System data exclusively to ORBCOMM and its government and commercial customers. The product is ship tracking and maritime navigational safety from orbit: AIS reports collected far beyond the roughly 50 km reach of shore stations, which is the baseline layer of any maritime domain awareness picture before radar or RF geolocation is added.

AAC HSI-SAT (EPICHYPER / DRAGONETTE).purpose: The EPICHyper satellites, known to their customer as Dragonette: 6U CubeSats designed, built, owned and operated by AAC Clyde Space that deliver hyperspectral imagery exclusively to the Canadian Earth observation company Wyvern under a Space Data as a Service contract. Hyperspectral imaging slices the reflected spectrum into many narrow bands rather than three broad colours, which is how a sensor distinguishes crop stress, invasive species and soil composition; Wyvern sells the data first into agriculture. The first of the three captures 23 bands at about 5.3 m pixels.

ABS.purpose: An ABS geostationary communications satellite. ABS operates a small five-satellite fleet from Dubai reaching the Americas, Africa, Asia-Pacific, Europe, the Middle East and northern Asia, selling data, broadcast and internet capacity with a stated focus on secure government communications and enterprise networks. Several of the spacecraft were bought second-hand and carry their previous names in the registry — ABS 4 was MBSAT, ABS 6 was LMI 1 — which is normal in this business and worth knowing when a catalogue entry and a footprint chart disagree about what a satellite is called.

ACCENTURE-1.purpose: A 3U CubeSat developed with Accenture and funded through ESA's Scale-up Invest programme in collaboration with the UK Space Agency, manufactured and integrated by Open Cosmos. It joins Open Cosmos's OpenConstellation - a shared infrastructure model in which several owners contribute satellites and all of them draw on the pooled data - and its role there is to process hyperspectral data in orbit for agriculture, energy and environmental management.

ADRAS-J.purpose: Astroscale's ADRAS-J, selected by JAXA for the first phase of its Commercial Removal of Debris Demonstration. It was the first attempt anywhere to approach and survey a real piece of large orbital debris, an abandoned Japanese rocket upper stage, using rendezvous and proximity operations, and it returned close-range imagery and dynamics data on an uncooperative object that was never designed to be approached. The same skill set underlies inspection of any non-cooperative satellite.

ADS-01 (OPTUS X).assessedBy: Gunter's Space Page and NextSpaceflight launch reporting
ADS-01 (OPTUS X).purpose: Catalogued as ADS-01 and identified in launch reporting as Optus-X, this is a geostationary communications satellite owned by Optus and built by Northrop Grumman Innovation Systems, understood to serve the Australian Defence Force. Neither manufacturer nor owner has published a payload description; the X in the name is read as pointing to a military X-band payload of the kind Optus and Defence previously flew together on C1. Treat the defence role as reported rather than declared.

AE.purpose: An ArkEdge Space micro-satellite, built on the Tokyo company's standardised 6U bus and flown to demonstrate satellite VDES, the VHF Data Exchange System. VDES is the two-way successor to AIS: the AE spacecraft carry deployable VHF antennas for wide-area, real-time vessel tracking and ship-to-shore data exchange, which for a maritime operator is the difference between collecting ship position reports and holding an actual data link with vessels at sea.

AE5R MARITIME RF.purpose: One of the three AE5R satellites ArkEdge Space launched together in late 2025. Unlike the company's VDES communications demonstrators these fly a radio-frequency observation payload aimed at maritime situational awareness: detecting and analysing the electromagnetic emissions of ships, which is how a vessel that is not transmitting AIS can still be located. The trio also exercises satellite-to-satellite handover so a constellation can hold a continuous link with the ground.

AEROSPACELAB VSP.purpose: A satellite on Aerospacelab's Versatile Satellite Platform, flown by the Belgian manufacturer both to prove its own bus and to carry radio-frequency sensing payloads. Aerospacelab's case for RF sensing is that optical imaging is limited by light and weather while a radio receiver is not, so mapping emissions from orbit — ship navigation radars, maritime and aeronautical communications, interference — fills in what a camera cannot see. Three of these four fly as an RF trio; ROSE is a separate demonstration on the same platform.

AETHER (KEPLER COMMUNICATIONS).purpose: Kepler Communications of Toronto operates Aether as an optical data-relay network in low Earth orbit - a mesh that routes other spacecraft's data between satellites by laser rather than waiting for a ground-station pass. Aether-1 and Aether-2 flew in November 2023 as pathfinders to validate the optical terminals; the first operational tranche of ten 300 kg-class satellites followed in January 2026, each with at least four optical terminals and communications built to be compatible with the US Space Development Agency's optical standards. The operational point for a military user is latency: an IP-routed relay ring gives near-real-time delivery from Earth-observation and defence payloads, including at high latitudes where ground-station geometry is worst.

AFR-1.purpose: ABA First Runner, the first satellite from Azista BST Aerospace, an Indo-German joint venture between Azista of Ahmedabad and Berlin Space Technologies. It is an 80 kg electro-optical spacecraft on the modular Azista-50 bus carrying a wide-swath, medium-resolution payload with both panchromatic and multispectral channels, sold as on-demand tasking for civilian and defence applications.

AGILA (ASTRANIS).purpose: An Astranis MicroGEO satellite - a roughly 400 kg geostationary comsat, small enough that four flew on one Falcon 9, and reprogrammable in orbit. Agila is the first communications satellite dedicated to the Philippines, flown in partnership with the regional service provider Orbits Corp to deliver broadband there. The MicroGEO model is worth understanding on its own terms: dedicated national capacity at a fraction of the cost and lead time of a conventional large geostationary spacecraft.

AII-BRAVO.purpose: AII-Bravo is a 6U CubeSat built by NanoAvionics in Vilnius to fly a spectrum-survey payload for the US company Aurora Insight - a proprietary spectrometer whose job is to measure the radio-frequency environment from orbit and produce usable maps of who is transmitting what, where. The mission is experimental, intended to qualify the instrument and prove that meaningful spectral measurements can be generated from a nanosatellite; SpaceQuest also used the flight to test a low-power VHF 'backdoor' receiver for recovering a wedged flight computer.

AISTECHSAT-2.purpose: AistechSat-2 is a 2U CubeSat flown by Aistech Space as the prototype for a tracking constellation, carrying an ADS-B receiver for space-based aircraft tracking together with a bidirectional store-and-forward link for automatic reporting from vessels and remote assets. Aistech claims it as the first European - and third worldwide - space-based air-traffic monitoring system. Space-based ADS-B matters for the same reason space-based AIS does: it puts aircraft outside radar and ground-station coverage, over ocean and remote terrain, back into a common operating picture.

AL YAH 3.purpose: Yahsat's all-Ka-band broadband satellite, and the odd one out in the fleet: instead of serving the Gulf it extends the operator's consumer and enterprise broadband into Africa and Brazil from 20 degrees West. It was the first hybrid electric propulsion GEOStar-3 spacecraft Orbital ATK completed, with Emirati engineers leading the project at each stage.

ALCOMSAT 1.purpose: Algeria's first geostationary communications satellite, ordered from China in 2013, built on the DFH-4 bus and operated by ASAL from control stations at Medea and Ouargla with Chinese-trained Algerian crews. It carries 33 transponders split between Ku and Ka-band for civil telecommunications and X-band, UHF and EHF capacity for military and strategic state users. That mixed civil and military payload on a single national satellite is the point of interest: Algeria bought sovereign military SATCOM and civil broadcast capacity in one spacecraft.

ALISIO-1.organization: IACTEC-Espacio, Instituto de Astrofisica de Canarias
ALISIO-1.purpose: ALISIO-1 - Advanced Land-Imaging Satellite for Infrared Observations - is the first satellite developed by the Instituto de Astrofisica de Canarias, built as a 6U CubeSat by Open Cosmos around the DRAGO-2 shortwave-infrared camera designed in-house by IACTEC-Espacio. DRAGO-2 works between about 1.0 and 1.7 microns at 50 m ground sampling, a band that sees through haze and reads moisture and thermal contrast, and the satellite has been used over the Canaries for vegetation, urban and spill monitoring. It also flew a CubeLCT laser communications terminal, making it the first Spanish satellite to demonstrate optical downlink.

ALMUNTHER.purpose: Al Munther, Bahrain's first domestically built satellite, developed by engineers at the kingdom's National Space Science Agency. It is a 3.2 kg nanosatellite, and what it demonstrates is national capability rather than payload capacity -- the first spacecraft the kingdom built rather than commissioned.

ALOS-2 DAICHI-2.purpose: Daichi-2, JAXA's L-band radar imaging satellite. Its PALSAR-2 radar images through cloud and darkness and the long L-band wavelength penetrates vegetation in a way X-band radars cannot, which is why Japan flies it for disaster response, forest survey and ground-deformation monitoring; a compact infrared camera alongside it measures land surface temperature and detects active fires. It also carries SPAISE2, JAXA's second-generation space-based AIS receiver, so the same spacecraft collects ship self-reporting data with its radar imagery.

ALOS-4 DAICHI-4.purpose: Daichi-4, the successor to ALOS-2 and Japan's current L-band radar imaging satellite. PALSAR-3 keeps the all-weather, day-night radar capability but widens the observing swath sharply, up to 200 km in stripmap and 700 km in ScanSAR, so far more ground is covered per pass for disaster, forest, sea-ice and infrastructure-displacement monitoring. Like its predecessor it carries a space-based AIS receiver, SPAISE3, to collect vessel reports over the ocean.

ALSAT 1B.purpose: A 100 kg medium-resolution Earth observation satellite built by Surrey Satellite Technology for the Algerian Space Agency and launched with Alsat-2B in September 2016. It complements the higher-resolution Alsat-2 pair with wide-swath imagery for agriculture, water resources and disaster response, and its commissioning was run jointly by SSTL and ASAL engineers as part of a deliberate skills-transfer programme.

ALSAT 2.purpose: The two identical high-resolution optical imaging satellites of Algeria's national space programme, operated by the Algerian Space Agency ASAL for cartography, agricultural and crop monitoring and disaster management. ASAL publishes their performance as 2.5 m panchromatic and 10 m multispectral across blue, green, red and near-infrared, with a three-day revisit over Algerian territory. Alsat-2B was placed 186 degrees out of phase with Alsat-2A so that the pair halves the revisit interval, and it is controlled from ASAL's satellite development centre at Oran.

ALSAT 3A.purpose: The first spacecraft of the Alsat-3 remote sensing system, contracted by the Algerian Space Agency to China Great Wall Industry Corporation in July 2023 and launched on a Long March 2C from Jiuquan in January 2026. It marks Algeria's switch from British to Chinese suppliers for its imaging line, having previously bought the Alsat-1 and Alsat-1B spacecraft from SSTL and Alsat-2 from Airbus. Detailed payload performance has not been published by ASAL.

AMAZONAS (HISPASAT).purpose: Despite the Brazilian registration, the Amazonas satellites are the Latin American arm of the Spanish operator Hispasat, flown mainly at 61 degrees West. Amazonas 2 and 3 carry C, Ku and Ka payloads over the whole American continent, Amazonas 3 being the first satellite to bring Ka-band to Latin America; Amazonas 4A suffered a power-subsystem failure shortly after launch that permanently cut its capacity; Amazonas 5 concentrates on Brazilian and Latin American television and Ka broadband. Amazonas Nexus replaced Amazonas 2 with a high-throughput payload and a digital transparent processor, and Hispasat sells it explicitly for air and maritime mobility, which is where a naval planner will meet it.

AMAZONIA 1.purpose: INPE describes Amazonia 1 as the first Earth observation satellite completely designed, integrated, tested and operated by Brazil, flying the national Multi-Mission Platform for the first time. Its wide-field imager covers three visible bands and one near-infrared band over an 850 km swath at 60 m resolution, deliberately traded for a five-day revisit so that deforestation alerts in the Amazon still get useful looks through persistent cloud. The imagery also feeds coastal, reservoir, agricultural and disaster monitoring, and the data are released to scientific and government users.

AMOS.purpose: Spacecom's AMOS fleet, Israel's commercial geostationary communications satellites. AMOS-3 works from 4 degrees West with Ku-band beams over Europe, the Middle East and North America; AMOS-4 sits at 65 degrees East covering Asia; AMOS-17 is a Boeing-built multi-band high-throughput spacecraft with Ka, Ku and C-band payloads at 17 degrees East, ordered to replace the AMOS-5 satellite that failed in orbit.

ANGOSAT 2.purpose: AngoSat-2 is Angola's geostationary communications satellite, carrying C-, Ku- and Ka-band capacity for telephony, broadband and television across Angola and much of Africa. It exists because AngoSat-1 did not: that spacecraft, launched in 2017, failed shortly after separation and was written off, and AngoSat-2 was built as its replacement — a Russian ISS Reshetnev bus carrying an Airbus payload. It is worth knowing as a case of what a national satellite programme actually costs a small state when the first attempt fails.

ANIK (TELESAT).purpose: Telesat's Anik fleet, the Canadian domestic geostationary comsats that have carried the country's long-haul television, telephony and data since the 1970s. Anik F2 was built to combine C-, Ku- and Ka-band on a single spacecraft, with C-band for satellite trunking into remote communities and Ka-band consumer broadband reaching the Far North, addressing the high-latitude problem that leaves northern Canada beyond the useful edge of most southern-pointed beams. Anik G1 adds broad single-beam coverage of South America plus what Telesat describes as the first commercial X-band payload covering the Americas, the Pacific Ocean and Hawaii for government users.

ANIK F1-R.purpose: A Telesat Anik: the Canadian domestic satellite series whose C- and Ku-band capacity carries broadcast, enterprise and government traffic across a country too large and too far north for terrestrial networks to reach economically. Anik F1R was built to replace the ageing Anik F1, and it also carries a hosted navigation package for the US Federal Aviation Administration's Wide Area Augmentation System, operating in C-band uplink and L-band downlink. That WAAS payload broadcasts GPS integrity and correction data over North America, so this spacecraft matters to anyone who depends on augmented GNSS rather than raw GPS for approach-grade positioning.

ANSER (INTA).purpose: An ANSER CubeSat - Advanced Nanosatellite Systems for Earth-observation Research - from Spain's INTA. Three 3U spacecraft fly as a cluster in a leader-follower formation, named for the wild goose, and behave as a single instrument: the leader commands the cluster and carries a panchromatic camera while the followers carry halves of a fragmented Cinclus hyperspectral photometer covering roughly 400 to 850 nm. They have no propulsion at all - relative station-keeping is done by deploying wing-like flaps that multiply the drag area and let each satellite surf the residual atmosphere. The science target is water quality in Iberian reservoirs and inland and coastal waters.

ARABSAT.purpose: The fleet of the Arab Satellite Communications Organization, founded in 1976 by the 21 member states of the Arab League and run from its headquarters in Riyadh with satellite control stations in Riyadh and Tunisia. Its satellites carry television, radio and data across the Middle East, Africa, Europe and Central Asia, with the 26 degrees East position serving as the regional direct-to-home hot spot. Individual spacecraft differ mainly by band and orbital slot -- Arabsat 5A carries C and Ku-band at 30.5 degrees East, Arabsat 5C carries C and Ka-band at 20 degrees East -- rather than by operator or purpose.

ARASE ERG.purpose: Arase, JAXA's Exploration of energization and Radiation in Geospace mission. It flies straight through the heart of the Van Allen belts to work out how radiation-belt electrons are accelerated past a million electron volts and how they are lost, by measuring the plasma waves and the charged particles together in the same place at the same time. That is the physics behind the internal-charging hazard that kills spacecraft electronics during geomagnetic storms, and behind the belt models operators rely on.

ARSAT.purpose: The first geostationary communications satellites built in Latin America, produced by the Argentine company INVAP for the state operator ARSAT and a deliberate act of orbital-slot sovereignty after Argentina came close to losing its ITU positions. ARSAT 1 holds 72 degrees West and ARSAT 2 holds 81 degrees West, carrying Ku and C-band telecommunications, data, telephony and television across Argentina, Chile, Uruguay and Paraguay and, from ARSAT's own service description, out to Antarctica and the South Atlantic islands. That southern reach is the operationally interesting part: it is the regional commercial capacity that covers the Drake Passage approaches.

ARVAKER.purpose: An Arvaker satellite, part of Norway's next-generation maritime surveillance constellation carrying AIS receivers and navigation-radar detection to succeed the NorSat and AISSat spacecraft. The rationale is the same one that produced its predecessors: Norway's area of maritime responsibility is enormous relative to its coastline and its fleet, and space is the only affordable way to see across it continuously.

ASBM.purpose: An Arctic Satellite Broadband Mission spacecraft. Geostationary satellites sit over the equator, so above roughly 75° North they are below the horizon and there is no broadband at all — which is why Space Norway put ASBM-1 and ASBM-2 into a highly elliptical three-apogee orbit, 8,100 km at perigee and 43,500 km at apogee, inclined 63° and phased so that one of the pair is always dwelling over the north. They carry payloads for the Norwegian Armed Forces, the U.S. Space Force and the commercial operator Viasat, and the American EPS-R payload was the first operational U.S. Department of Defense payload ever hosted on a foreign spacecraft. For anyone planning operations above the Arctic Circle this is the communications architecture that makes them possible.

ASIASAT.purpose: An AsiaSat geostationary communications satellite. AsiaSat is a Hong Kong operator whose C- and Ku-band spacecraft cover about two thirds of the world's population from the Middle East across South and East Asia to Australasia, carrying television distribution, telecom trunking and maritime and aeronautical mobility capacity. Its wide C-band beams are among the more useful commercial footprints over the South China Sea and the eastern Indian Ocean, where rain fade makes Ku-band unreliable.

ASNARO.organization: NEC / Japan Space Systems, for METI
ASNARO.purpose: An ASNARO spacecraft, the Advanced Satellite with New system ARchitecture for Observation, developed by NEC with Japan Space Systems under Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry sponsorship to prove that a 400 kg-class satellite could match the performance of a medium or large commercial imager, at better than 0.5 m ground sampling distance, and be sold abroad. The two spacecraft are a deliberate pair, one optical and one radar, flying at different local times so their measurements complement each other.

ASTRA.purpose: An Astra geostationary satellite: SES's European broadcast fleet, clustered at a handful of orbital positions — chiefly 19.2° East and 28.2° East — so that a fixed dish anywhere in Europe can see several spacecraft without moving. Astra began in 1988 as the pan-European direct-to-home television system and is now operated directly by SES; the newer spacecraft carry data and broadband payloads alongside the television transponders. Astra 1P is also catalogued as SES 24, which is why the same spacecraft appears under two names in some sources.

ASTRANIS UTILITYSAT.purpose: Astranis's multi-mission MicroGEO spacecraft, built to be reconfigured in orbit and moved between customers over its life rather than serving one contract from one slot. Its first task was to stand in for services lost when Astranis's first satellite, Arcturus, suffered a solar array drive failure in 2023; its first named customer is Mexico's APCO Networks. A geostationary asset that can be repointed and reprogrammed to a different mission is an unusual thing in this catalog and the reason the spacecraft is named the way it is.

ASTROCAST.purpose: An Astrocast nanosatellite: a Swiss low-Earth-orbit constellation carrying store-and-forward L-band messaging for the Internet of Things — the low-rate, low-power, high-latency traffic that comes off buoys, containers, livestock, pipelines and small vessels where there is no cellular coverage and a broadband terminal makes no sense. The design accepts minutes or hours of delivery delay in exchange for terminals that cost tens of dollars and run for years on a battery.

ASTROSAT.purpose: India's first dedicated space astronomy observatory, and unusual in being able to observe one object simultaneously from the far ultraviolet through the optical to hard X-rays above 100 keV. It carries five instruments, including UVIT, whose 1.5 arcsecond resolution ISRO records as three times better than the next best ultraviolet telescope then flying; the large-area LAXPC X-ray counters; and the CZTI, which can measure X-ray polarisation. It is run as a national observatory with observing time allocated to Indian and international astronomers.

AUSTRIA PRETTY.organization: European Space Agency / Beyond Gravity Austria / TU Graz
AUSTRIA PRETTY.purpose: PRETTY (Passive REflecTomeTry and dosimetrY) is an Austrian 3U cubesat that measures the Earth by catching GNSS signals reflected off it. The strength and shape of a reflected navigation signal depends on the roughness of the surface it bounced from, which gives sea state and significant wave height over open water and ice extent and type over the poles — measurements normally requiring a radar altimeter, obtained here with a receiver and no transmitter at all. It also carries a radiation dosimeter to characterise the orbital environment.

AUTCUBE 2.purpose: A 1U CubeSat built by Japan's Aichi University of Technology and nicknamed Gamacube. Its four objectives were to establish very low power satellite communications using a transmitter of one milliwatt or less with the WSJT weak-signal protocol, to study electromagnetic interference at the command uplink frequency with an onboard narrowband spectrum analyser, to test optical communications using high-power LEDs, and to capture virtual-reality content with two fisheye cameras. It is a student technology mission with no operational role.

AZALEA CLUSTER 1 (AC1).assessedBy: Gunter's Space Page, drawing on BAE Systems and In-Space Missions programme statements
AZALEA CLUSTER 1 (AC1).purpose: Azalea Cluster 1, a multi-sensor cluster developed by BAE Systems in the UK to collect radio-frequency emissions alongside synthetic aperture radar and other sensor data, process it on orbit, and deliver near-real-time intelligence products. The satellites are synchronised through inter-satellite links so that the cluster can geolocate an RF emitter precisely while simultaneously imaging the scene around it - the combination that turns a detected transmission into an identified vessel or vehicle. Tasking and command across the constellation run through a coordinating Azalea Hub. The individual sensor specifications are not published.

AZERSPACE.purpose: Azerbaijan's national satellite communications fleet, operated by Azercosmos. Azerspace-1 at 46 degrees East was the country's first satellite, an Orbital Sciences Star-2.4 spacecraft covering Europe, Africa, Central Asia, the Middle East and the Caucasus for television, radio and internet. Azerspace-2 flies at 45 degrees East as a shared programme with Intelsat, where the same spacecraft is also Intelsat 38 -- a common way for a small national operator to afford a second satellite.

Aistech Hydra.purpose: A Hydra satellite of the Barcelona company Aistech Space, whose business is detecting, tracking and monitoring temperature changes on the Earth's surface. Hydra 2 opened the commercial constellation and was the first to carry the Multispectral Thermal Telescope Aistech developed in-house, a step up in resolution from the company's earlier demonstrators. Thermal infrared is the band that keeps working at night and through smoke and haze, which is why a thermal revisit is useful for wildfire, industrial and infrastructure activity monitoring, and why Aistech markets the constellation to security users as well as environmental ones.

Apogeo Space PICO.purpose: A PICO spacecraft from Apogeo Space, a Brescia company building what it describes as the first private Italian satellite constellation - picosatellites of well under a kilogram, flown in numbers, to carry Internet-of-Things traffic from low-power sensors in places with no terrestrial coverage. The service is designed to be hybrid: the picosatellite constellation provides the global layer while ground 'satellite boosters' thicken coverage over specific areas a customer cares about.

BADR.purpose: The Badr satellites are Arabsat's direct-to-home broadcasting constellation, co-located at the 26 degrees East video hot spot so that one fixed dish sees the entire line-up -- the reason an operator keeps adding spacecraft to the same slot rather than spreading them out. Badr 7, also designated Arabsat 6B, is a Eurostar-3000 built by Astrium and Thales Alenia Space carrying 24 Ku-band transponders together with 24 Ka-band spot beams and three Ka-band transponders.

BANGABANDHUSAT-1.purpose: Bangladesh's first satellite, a Thales Alenia Space Spacebus-4000B2 communications and broadcasting spacecraft operated by the state-owned Bangladesh Satellite Company Limited. Thales built it, delivered it in orbit and supplied both the primary and backup ground segments; its declared purpose is to narrow the digital divide by carrying broadcasting and telecommunications into rural Bangladesh and to sell direct-to-home and regional services. It also happened to be the first payload flown by a Falcon 9 Block 5.

BEE-1000.purpose: A space-medical 6U cubesat flown on Nuri's fourth launch. Its payload, BEE-PC1 from Space LiinTech, is a 4U module containing a protein crystal growth chamber that controls and monitors how the crystals form; without convection to disturb them, crystals grown in microgravity give cleaner X-ray structures for drug design than the same proteins grown on the ground. The Department of Satellite Systems at Yonsei University designed, built and integrated the cubesat bus.

BELINTERSAT 1.purpose: Belintersat-1 is Belarus's only communications satellite: a Chinese DFH-4 bus with a Thales Alenia Space payload, built by CAST, launched from Xichang in 2016 and stationed at 51.5° East. It carries 38 C- and Ku-band transponders covering eastern Europe, central and eastern Asia and Africa, and part of its capacity is sold to China Satcom, where the same spacecraft is marketed as ChinaSat 15. A satellite with a Belarusian owner, a Chinese platform and launch, a French payload and Chinese resale is a fair picture of how national space capability is assembled outside the major powers.

BLACK KITE.purpose: An 8U IoT CubeSat built by Rapidtek Technologies of Taipei, commissioned by the Taiwan Space Agency and developed with the Industrial Technology Research Institute. It is the start of Rapidtek's low-orbit constellation for satellite Internet-of-Things service — machine-to-machine reporting from assets outside terrestrial network coverage, which at sea means unattended sensors and small craft.

BLUEBON.purpose: BlueBON is a joint Korean-Polish mission - payload and software by TelePIX, 6U-XL platform and mission operations from Wroclaw by SatRev - built to measure blue carbon, the carbon sequestered by marine ecosystems. Its multispectral camera is tuned to pick out floating algae, and the TetraPLEX onboard AI processor runs TelePIX's BlueSCOPE analysis in orbit to detect the algae and estimate the carbon they hold, rather than downlinking raw scenes for processing later.

BOTSAT-1.organization: Botswana International University of Science and Technology
BOTSAT-1.purpose: BOTSAT-1 is Botswana's first satellite, a 3U cubesat carrying a hyperspectral imager, built by EnduroSat of Bulgaria with engineers from the Botswana International University of Science and Technology and launched in March 2025. It is a national capability-building project as much as a data mission: the government of Botswana funded it through BIUST to establish a domestic space engineering base, and the hyperspectral payload is aimed at mineral prospecting and land and water monitoring.

BRISAT.purpose: BRIsat is the first satellite owned and operated by a bank. Bank Rakyat Indonesia bought it to carry its own transaction and branch networking traffic to more than ten thousand branches and thousands of ATMs across the archipelago, on the reasoning that owning the spacecraft was cheaper than the roughly 500 billion rupiah a year it had been paying to lease capacity. It is a communications satellite in the ordinary technical sense, but an unusual case of a non-telecoms company becoming its own satellite operator.

BRITE TORONTO.purpose: One of the Canadian members of BRITE-Constellation, an Austrian-Canadian-Polish network of nanosatellites that performs two-colour precision photometry of the very brightest stars in the sky. Each 7 kg spacecraft carries a 3 cm telescope feeding an uncooled CCD, one of each pair filtered blue and the other red, and the targets are the massive luminous stars whose winds and supernovae seed the galaxy with heavy elements. It was the first space astronomy mission flown with nanosatellites.

BRITE-AUSTRIA TUGSAT-1.purpose: BRITE-Austria, also called TUGSAT-1, was Austria's first satellite and is one member of BRITE-Constellation, a network of nanosatellites built by Austrian, Canadian and Polish groups to measure the brightness of the very brightest stars in the sky to high precision, in red and blue. Those stars are too bright for most large telescopes to observe without saturating, so a small dedicated instrument is genuinely the right tool; the variations it records reveal the internal structure, pulsation and winds of massive stars.

BRITE-PL 2.organization: Space Research Centre of the Polish Academy of Sciences
BRITE-PL 2.purpose: BRITE-PL 2 is Heweliusz, the second Polish contribution to BRITE-Constellation - BRIght Target Explorer - a fleet of six 7 kg, 20 cm nanosatellites built on Canadian technology by Canada, Austria and Poland as equal partners, with the Polish units built by the Space Research Centre of the Polish Academy of Sciences and operated by the Copernicus Astronomical Centre. Each carries a wide-field telescope, roughly 24 degrees across, that measures brightness and temperature variations of the brightest stars over hours to months - a photometric time series of a precision the atmosphere makes impossible from the ground, used to study stellar winds and to age luminous stars by asteroseismology.

BRO.purpose: A BRO (Breizh Reconnaissance Orbiter) satellite: Unseenlabs, a French company based in Rennes, flies these to detect and geolocate the radio-frequency emissions of ships at sea. The premise is that a vessel intent on not being seen can switch off its AIS transponder, but it cannot switch off everything — navigation radar, VHF, VSAT and the rest keep radiating — and each emitter has a signature that can be characterised and matched across passes. That gives a picture of what is on the water regardless of cloud, darkness or whether the vessel is cooperating, which is what AIS cannot do and what optical and SAR imaging can only do where they happen to be looking. Unseenlabs describes it as data that complements AIS, VMS, SAR and optical rather than replacing them, and that is the honest reading: RF geolocation tells you something is emitting from roughly there, and it takes a second sensor to say what it is. Each spacecraft is a smallsat carrying a single wide-band RF payload, so the constellation's revisit — not any one satellite — is the capability.

BSAT.purpose: A BSAT broadcasting satellite of B-SAT Corporation, the company that carries Japan's BS direct-to-home television. B-SAT keeps a set of spacecraft co-located at 110 degrees East covering the whole country, deliberately more than the traffic requires, so that a failure in orbit does not take national broadcasting off the air; the newer BSAT-4 pair carry the 4K and 8K satellite services. Direct broadcast from orbit survives earthquakes and other disasters that cut terrestrial distribution, which is why the system is treated as emergency information infrastructure.

BUCCANEER MAIN MISSION.purpose: Buccaneer Main Mission is an Australian Defence nanosatellite built by the Defence Science and Technology Group, and it exists to solve a specifically Australian radar problem: it deploys a large high-frequency antenna and operates an HF receiver to contribute to the calibration of the Jindalee Operational Radar Network, the over-the-horizon radar that watches Australia's northern approaches. Because OTH radar performance depends entirely on the state of the ionosphere it bounces off, the satellite's decade of high-frequency measurements of radio propagation through the ionosphere is space-weather data with an immediate operational consumer. A secondary optical payload, MANTIS, verifies the HF antenna actually deployed and images the Earth through a 3D-printed rotatable mirror.

BUGSAT 1.purpose: Also called Tita, a 22 kg technology demonstrator flown by the Argentine company Satellogic as the precursor to its Aleph-1 (NuSat) Earth observation constellation. It tested custom antennas, a mid-resolution camera, a GPS receiver and UHF and C-band radios built from commercial off-the-shelf parts, and after the demonstration phase it transmitted AX.25 packets and acted as a digipeater for the amateur radio community. It is the flight that established the low-cost imaging bus Satellogic later scaled up commercially.

BULGARIASAT-1.purpose: BulgariaSat-1 is the first Bulgarian geostationary satellite, built by Space Systems/Loral on the SSL 1300 bus for the operator Bulgaria Sat and stationed at 1.9 degrees East. It carries 30 Ku-band broadcasting-service transponders and three Ku-band fixed-service transponders, serving direct-to-home television, VSAT and satellite news gathering across the Balkans and into central and western Europe.

Balkan Constellation.purpose: A Balkan satellite from the Sofia manufacturer EnduroSat: 16U nanosatellites imaging in seven multispectral bands plus panchromatic between 450 and 900 nm at about 1.5 m ground sampling over a 14 km swath, selected by ESA and the EU as a Copernicus Contributing Mission. EnduroSat leads its own application list with maritime surveillance - detecting vessels and suspicious activity and tracking maritime traffic in near real time using AI processing performed on board, in support of border surveillance and supply-chain monitoring - with emergency mapping and vegetation monitoring behind it.

CANX-2.purpose: A Canadian Advanced Nanospace eXperiment nanosatellite from the University of Toronto Institute for Aerospace Studies Space Flight Laboratory. CanX-2 was the technology-qualification flight whose subsystems were then reused to fly the CanX-4/CanX-5 formation-flying mission, so its value was proving the bus, the GPS receiver and the ground segment rather than any single payload.

CANX-4 / CANX-5.purpose: A pair of identical Canadian nanosatellites that demonstrated autonomous formation flight at a scale nobody had achieved before at this class. Using carrier-phase differential GPS, a cold-gas propulsion system and an inter-satellite radio link, they held formations to better than one metre with relative position knowledge of a few centimetres, at ranges from 1000 m down to 50 m, and the German Aerospace Center independently verified the results. The reason a naval reader should care is what precise formation flight enables downstream: sparse-aperture sensing, ground moving target indication and precise emitter geolocation all depend on knowing where several small spacecraft are relative to each other.

CARBONITE 1.purpose: An SSTL technology demonstrator built to prove video from orbit and rapid-build methods, designed, built and tested in six months and twelve days using commercial off-the-shelf components. Its adapted industrial video camera produced 15-second high-definition clips at about 1 m ground sample distance; SSTL released footage of an aircraft taxiing in Kuwait and traffic moving in Dubai. The mission's real product was the cost and schedule model that led to Carbonite-2 and to the Carbonite platform later reused for CarbSAR.

CARBSAR.organization: Surrey Satellite Technology Ltd / Oxford Space Systems
CARBSAR.purpose: An in-orbit demonstration of high-resolution X-band synthetic aperture radar from a 140 kg spacecraft, built by SSTL on the Carbonite platform around Oxford Space Systems' Wrapped Rib deployable antenna - the first large deployable reflector OSS has flown. SSTL quotes 0.5 m ground resolution over a 4 km swath in spotlight mode, day or night and through weather, and lists defence and security, maritime, disaster response and infrastructure as the target applications. The antenna deployed successfully in January 2026.

CAS500 NATIONAL LAND SATELLITES.organization: KARI / Korea Aerospace Industries / National Geographic Information Institute
CAS500 NATIONAL LAND SATELLITES.purpose: The two National Land Satellites of the Compact Advanced Satellite 500 series, developed by KARI with Korea Aerospace Industries and operated through the National Geographic Information Institute. Each carries a high-resolution electro-optical sensor giving 0.5 m panchromatic and 2 m multispectral imagery over a swath of at least 12 km, used for land and natural-resource management, disaster monitoring and national spatial information. The series exists so Korea can develop satellites for its own public demand rather than buy them, and CAS500-2 was the first of the pair built under industry technology transfer.

CAS500-3.organization: Korea Aerospace Industries / Ministry of Science and ICT
CAS500-3.purpose: The odd one out in the CAS500 series: not an imaging satellite but a space-science and technology-verification platform for the Ministry of Science and ICT, built by Korea Aerospace Industries and flown as the primary payload of Nuri's fourth launch. It carries a wide-field camera for auroras and other atmospheric light, an instrument tracking changes in charged particles around Earth, and a device testing 3D bio-printing of stem cells in microgravity. All three reported healthy in their first weeks of operation.

CAS500-4.organization: Korea Aerospace Industries / Rural Development Administration / Korea Forest Service
CAS500-4.purpose: Korea's first Earth-observation satellite dedicated to agriculture and forestry, built by Korea Aerospace Industries for use by the Rural Development Administration and the Korea Forest Service. Its wide-swath camera trades resolution for coverage - 5 m detail across a 120 km strip - so it images the entire Korean Peninsula in three passes. The data goes to crop growth and yield analysis, greenhouse-gas estimation and forest-resource monitoring, and to wildfire and forest-damage response.

CASSIOPE (SWARM-ECHO).organization: Canadian Space Agency / University of Calgary
CASSIOPE (SWARM-ECHO).purpose: CASSIOPE is Canada's hybrid small satellite and, for a space-weather audience, one of the more directly relevant objects in this catalog. Its e-POP payload - the Enhanced Polar Outflow Probe, eight instruments including plasma imagers, radio receivers, magnetometers and cameras, operated by the University of Calgary - measures the topside ionosphere and the plasma outflows driven by space storms, precisely the disturbances that degrade HF communications and GNSS navigation. Its elliptical polar orbit carries it repeatedly through the auroral zone, and in 2018 ESA adopted it into the Swarm mission as Swarm-Echo, a fourth element alongside Alpha, Bravo and Charlie. A second payload, MDA's Cascade store-and-forward communications demonstrator, was decommissioned in late 2015.

CE-SAT-IE.purpose: A 70 kg imaging satellite built by Canon Electronics around its own camera technology. Its primary telescope pairs a 40 cm mirror with an optical sensor derived from the commercial Canon EOS R5 body, and it returns roughly 0.8 m ground sampling distance over a scene a few kilometres across. The interest of the spacecraft is the method: commercial off-the-shelf camera hardware, rolling shutter and all, calibrated to survey-grade geometric accuracy.

CENTAURI (FLEET SPACE).purpose: Fleet Space Technologies of Adelaide flies the Centauri satellites as Australia's first commercial low-orbit constellation, providing narrowband connectivity for remote sensors. Their principal commercial use is ExoSphere, Fleet's end-to-end mineral exploration system, in which ground seismic sensors deployed across a survey area report through the satellites and are processed into three-dimensional subsurface images. The company also markets the same network for defence connectivity; the underlying capability is low-power machine-to-machine backhaul from places with no terrestrial infrastructure.

CHAMRAN-1.purpose: An Iranian technology demonstration satellite whose declared mission is to test hardware and software systems, specifically demonstrating orbital manoeuvring in altitude and phase, along with a cold-gas propulsion subsystem and navigation and attitude control performance. Iranian media subsequently reported that it carried out a rendezvous exercise with the spent Qaem-100 launcher body. Manoeuvre and rendezvous demonstrations are inherently dual-use, and the reported results have not been independently verified.

CMS.purpose: India's Communication Multi-band Satellite series, the designation ISRO adopted for its operational geostationary comsats after the GSAT numbering. CMS-01 provides Extended-C band capacity whose coverage takes in the Indian mainland together with the Andaman-Nicobar and Lakshadweep island groups -- the band and footprint used for long-haul trunking and broadcast feeds into remote territory, where rain fade on higher bands is the limiting factor.

CMS 03.purpose: The heaviest communications satellite ever launched to geostationary transfer orbit from Indian soil, and a multi-band spacecraft that ISRO says will provide services over a wide oceanic region including the Indian landmass. That is word for word the phrasing ISRO uses for GSAT-7, the Navy's Rukmini, and it describes an ocean-area SATCOM footprint rather than a landmass broadcasting one.

CO3D.purpose: A CO3D (Constellation Optique en 3D) satellite: four roughly 300 kg spacecraft flown by CNES and Airbus together, working in stereo pairs to build a worldwide digital surface model at about one metre accuracy. A global elevation model of that quality is infrastructure rather than imagery — it is what line-of-sight, radio propagation, flood, landing-zone and terrain-masking analysis are computed against, and until now the best global models have been an order of magnitude coarser. The satellites are all-electric and highly agile, so the same platforms also return conventional high-resolution optical imagery.

COMS 1.purpose: Chollian, Korea's first geostationary multi-purpose satellite, developed by KARI with the Korea Meteorological Administration and partners to do meteorology, ocean observation and communications from one platform. Its Meteorological Imager supplied cloud, humidity, atmospheric-wind and sea-surface-temperature fields over the Korean peninsula, while the Geostationary Ocean Colour Imager watched coastal water and ocean biology - putting SST and ocean colour on the same continuously staring spacecraft is exactly what a METOC watch floor wants. The meteorological mission ended in March 2020 and the ocean mission in March 2021, with the work passed to GEO-KOMPSAT-2; the communications payload is still in use.

CONNECTA.purpose: A Connecta satellite: the 6U-class low-Earth-orbit Internet-of-Things constellation designed, built and operated by the Turkish company Plan-S through its wholly owned subsidiary Connecta Communication Services. The service is narrowband machine-to-machine connectivity for sensors and remote assets that sit outside terrestrial cellular coverage, and Connecta holds the first licence Turkiye's telecoms regulator (BTK) has issued to a LEO satellite operator, with the constellation planned to grow towards 200 spacecraft. The early T1.2 spacecraft flew a software-defined radio payload so that new waveforms could be uploaded in orbit, making it an experimental testbed rather than an operational node.

CONTECSAT-1.purpose: Also called Oreum, a 16U cubesat that opens the Korean company Contec's constellation of high-resolution Earth imaging satellites. Contec states three targets for it: monitoring urban change, monitoring maritime activity, and predicting crop yields. Maritime activity monitoring from a small optical satellite in practice means routine looks at ports, anchorages and coastal traffic on a revisit a single spacecraft cannot yet sustain - hence the constellation.

COSMO-SkyMed.organization: Italian Space Agency (ASI) / Italian Ministry of Defence
COSMO-SkyMed.purpose: A first-generation COSMO-SkyMed spacecraft - the name stands for COnstellation of small Satellites for the Mediterranean basin Observation - the four-satellite Italian X-band synthetic aperture radar constellation owned and operated by ASI and funded jointly by the Italian ministries of research and of defence. It is an explicitly dual civil-military system: the same radar that maps earthquakes, volcanoes and floods does all-weather, day-and-night maritime surveillance, ship detection, oil-spill and sea-ice work, which is why COSMO-SkyMed imagery turns up routinely in Mediterranean maritime-domain-awareness products. A single satellite revisits a target in about five days; the full constellation cuts that to hours.

COSMO-SkyMed Second Generation.organization: Italian Space Agency (ASI) / Italian Ministry of Defence
COSMO-SkyMed Second Generation.purpose: A COSMO-SkyMed Second Generation (CSG) satellite - the catalogue lists the third flight model as COSMO-SKYMED-FM3 - continuing Italy's X-band SAR constellation with a more capable radar built by Thales Alenia Space for ASI, the Ministry of Defence and the research ministry. Like the first generation it is declared a dual system, civil and military, and its published mission list names defence, security and maritime surveillance alongside risk management and cartography; the SAR works in modes ranging from ultrafine narrow-field to wide-swath, so an operator can trade resolution against area on the same pass. For a maritime watch officer the practical value is all-weather ship detection and interferometric change detection over a 16-day repeat cycle.

CROCUBE.purpose: CroCube is Croatia's first satellite: a 1U cubesat built by a Croatian educational society and launched in December 2024, carrying an amateur-radio payload for radio amateurs and for students working toward their licences. It is a technology demonstrator and an education project rather than an operational asset, and that is the point of it — a first national satellite is usually about building the people and the ground station, not the data.

CUAVA-2.purpose: A 6U CubeSat from the ARC Training Centre for CubeSats, UAVs and Their Applications at the University of Sydney, carrying eight research payloads with remote sensing, Earth observation and space weather as its declared foci. Among them is Harry3, a GPS-reflectometry receiver from UNSW's Australian Centre for Space Engineering Research that measures GPS signals scattered off the surface to retrieve ocean wave conditions and to discriminate sea ice - directly relevant to shipping and offshore operations. The satellite took radiation damage after deployment, but identical payloads flown on Waratah Seed-1 preserved most of the mission's results.

CUBEBUG 2.organization: Argentine Ministry of Science, Technology and Productive Innovation
CUBEBUG 2.purpose: Nicknamed Manolito, the second demonstration flight of an Argentine 2U CubeSat platform whose mechanics, hardware and software were deliberately released as open source and open hardware for amateur, university and research use. Sponsored by the Argentine Ministry of Science with INVAP, Satellogic and Radio Club Bariloche, it flight-tested an antenna, solar panels, an on-board computer, a camera, a GPS unit and a software-defined radio built from commercial parts, and carries an AX.25 packet digipeater for amateur operators.

CUBESAT XI.purpose: XI-IV and XI-V, the picosatellites of the Intelligent Space Systems Laboratory at the University of Tokyo. XI-IV was one of the first CubeSats ever launched and established the basic technologies for the class; XI-V followed to demonstrate new hardware in orbit, including verification of copper indium gallium diselenide thin-film solar cells. Both were built from commercial off-the-shelf parts, the point being to show that useful spacecraft could be produced quickly and cheaply by students.

CUTE TITECH.purpose: A CUTE spacecraft — Cubical Titech Engineering Satellite — from the Laboratory for Space Systems at the Tokyo Institute of Technology. CUTE-I proved a student-built CubeSat could hold a communications link, characterise its own thermal and dynamic environment in orbit and deploy a solar paddle on command; CUTE-1.7+APD carried an avalanche photodiode radiation detector built by another Tokyo Tech laboratory.

DIWATA.organization: Philippine Space Agency / University of the Philippines Diliman
DIWATA.purpose: A Diwata microsatellite: the Philippines' first home-built Earth-observation spacecraft, designed and assembled by Filipino researchers at the University of the Philippines Diliman and DOST-ASTI with Tohoku and Hokkaido Universities under the PHL-Microsat programme. Diwata-2 carries a spaceborne multispectral imager and a high-precision telescope for agriculture, disaster assessment and weather work over the archipelago, together with an amateur-radio unit intended as an emergency communications relay after typhoons — a capability with obvious value in a country that takes about twenty a year.

DJIBOUTI-1B.organization: Centre d'Etude et de Recherche de Djibouti
DJIBOUTI-1B.purpose: Djibouti's second nanosatellite, launched in December 2024 and developed with the Space Center of the University of Montpellier as part of a national programme built around training Djiboutian students. Its purpose is to enhance climate monitoring under the Hydrosat initiative: working with its predecessor Djibouti-1A, it gathers data used to track water resource availability and assess drought-affected regions. For a small state on the Bab el-Mandeb it is a deliberately cheap first step into sovereign space capability.

DLR ENMAP.purpose: EnMAP — the Environmental Mapping and Analysis Program — is a German hyperspectral imaging satellite that records more than two hundred contiguous narrow bands from the visible into the shortwave infrared. That much spectral detail turns imagery into a measurement of material: mineral composition, vegetation stress and species, water constituents, and soil condition can be identified from the shape of a spectrum rather than inferred from colour. The data are distributed free for scientific use.

DLR EUCROPIS.purpose: Eu:CROPIS is a DLR satellite that spins about its long axis to generate artificial gravity, holding lunar levels for part of the mission and Martian levels for the rest, while two sealed greenhouses inside try to run a closed biological life-support loop: synthetic urine converted by biofilters into fertiliser, dwarf tomatoes grown on it, algae maintaining the atmosphere. The question it exists to answer is whether such a loop stays stable for months at reduced gravity, which is a prerequisite for any long-duration crewed mission that does not resupply from Earth.

DMC 2 (UK-DMC-2).purpose: The United Kingdom's contribution to the Disaster Monitoring Constellation, a set of SSTL-built imagers each owned by a different national partner and coordinated by DMC International Imaging. The design trade is unusual and deliberate: a very wide 650 km swath at moderate resolution, cross-calibrated to within about 1% of Landsat, so that a single pass can cover a whole flood or fire in one frame and be handed straight to analysts already trained on Landsat products. The constellation is a formal contributor to the International Charter Space and Major Disasters. UK-DMC-2 carried the SLIM-6-22 multispectral imager at 22 m ground sample distance.

DMC 3 / TRIPLESAT.purpose: Three identical SSTL-300S1 satellites flown as the TripleSat constellation, phased 120 degrees apart so that any point on Earth can be targeted daily with up to 45 degrees of off-pointing. Each carries a pushbroom imager delivering 1 m panchromatic and 4 m multispectral imagery over a roughly 24 km swath, and the whole imaging capacity is leased to the Beijing commercial imaging company 21AT. The daily revisit is what makes them useful for change detection and disaster response rather than mapping alone.

DOORY-SAT.organization: Hanwha Systems / Agency for Defense Development
DOORY-SAT.purpose: Formerly S-STEP 1, the Small SAR Technology Experimental Project: a roughly 100 kg flat-panel radar satellite built by Hanwha Systems as the prototype for a future Korean constellation, and launched on the Agency for Defense Development's own solid-propellant test vehicle from a sea platform off Jeju. Its X-band radar works in stripmap, ScanSAR and VideoSAR modes at metre-class resolution, downlinks at 1 Gbps and carries an S-band inter-satellite link. That combination - cheap, flat, radar, networked - is what a constellation needs to hold ships and coastline under watch through cloud and darkness.

DRISHTI.purpose: GalaxEye's first satellite and, the company says, the first to combine a multispectral imager and a synthetic aperture radar on one platform, so that the optical and radar products are inherently co-registered rather than aligned afterwards. Quoted resolution across the combined SAR and MSI products is 1.2 to 3.6 m. Fusing the two attacks the all-weather problem directly: the radar keeps working through cloud and at night, while the optical channel supplies the interpretation a radar image alone does not give.

DROR-1.purpose: Israel's first state-owned national communications satellite, fully developed and manufactured by Israel Aerospace Industries and presented by the Israeli government as a step towards full communications independence for the state. Where the AMOS satellites are commercially owned and operated, Dror-1 is a national asset carrying technologies developed in Israel.

DRUMS KHI.purpose: DRUMS, the Debris Removal Unprecedented Micro Satellite, developed in-house by Kawasaki Heavy Industries and selected as a demonstration theme on JAXA's second Innovative Satellite Technology Demonstration flight. Its plan was to release a target of its own, then autonomously track and approach it and extend an arm to simulate capture — the close-approach problem that any debris removal or satellite servicing operation has to solve first.

DS-EO.purpose: A Singaporean electro-optical imaging satellite acquired by ST Engineering with the Defence Science and Technology Agency and built by South Korea's Satrec Initiative, carrying a multispectral payload with 0.5 m resolution. Its declared users are Singapore government agencies, with maritime security and oil-spill detection named explicitly, and the surplus capacity feeds ST Engineering's commercial imagery business. For a Singapore-based navy that is a half-metre look at the Strait of Malacca and Singapore Strait approaches under national tasking control.

DSN-3 KIRAMEKI-3.organization: DSN Corporation, for the Japanese Ministry of Defense
DSN-3 KIRAMEKI-3.purpose: Kirameki-3, the third X-band defence communications satellite in Japan's military SATCOM system. It is built and operated by DSN Corporation, a joint venture of SKY Perfect JSAT, NEC and NTT Communications, under a programme contract with the Ministry of Defense to upgrade and run Japan's X-band satellite communications function. The Ministry describes X-band defence communications satellites as the means of communicating with forces at long range; the specific capacity, coverage and hardening of this spacecraft are not published.

DTUSAT 2.purpose: DTUsat-2 is a 1U cubesat built by students and staff at DTU Space to track migrating birds from orbit. The payload is a receiver for miniature radio transmitters fitted to the birds before migration — an idea that only works if the space segment can hear a fraction of a watt from a moving animal, which is precisely what the mission set out to establish.

DUBAISAT.purpose: The UAE's first two Earth observation satellites, built with Satrec Initiative of South Korea for what is now the Mohammed bin Rashid Space Centre. DubaiSat-1 carried the Dubai Medium Aperture Camera on Satrec's SI-200 bus and DubaiSat-2 continued the programme with a sharper instrument. They were the apprenticeship that produced KhalifaSat, the first UAE satellite built at home.

DUCHIFAT 1.purpose: A 1U cubesat built by secondary school students at the Space Laboratory of the Herzliya Science Centre. Its mission is to relay Automatic Position Reporting System packets from low Earth orbit, so that travellers, boats at sea and stations far from terrestrial APRS infrastructure can report position and exchange short messages using ordinary handheld amateur radios -- a store-and-forward safety and messaging service on a spacecraft the size of a coffee mug.

DUTHSAT-2.organization: Democritus University of Thrace / Hellenic Space Center
DUTHSAT-2.purpose: DUTHSat-2 is a 6U CubeSat built by the Democritus University of Thrace with Greek and ESA support, and the first mission flown under ESA's Greek CubeSat In-Orbit Validation programme. It returns visible and near-infrared imagery aimed at soil-moisture monitoring ashore and oil-spill and water-pollution detection at sea, and also flies an Essential TeleMetry unit - a black-box-like recorder for spacecraft.

Deimos (GEOSAT).purpose: A Deimos optical imaging satellite, Spain's first commercial Earth-observation spacecraft. Deimos-1 was built by Surrey Satellite Technology on the SSTL-100 bus for Elecnor Deimos and flies as a member of the Disaster Monitoring Constellation, contributing wide-swath medium-resolution imagery to disaster response; Deimos-2 followed in 2014 as the higher-resolution companion. Both passed to UrtheCast and then, in 2021, to GEOSAT, under which Deimos-1 was renamed GEOSAT-1 and its data continues to be distributed through ESA's Third Party Missions programme.

E-SPACE CALISTUS.assessedBy: Gunter's Space Page, which records the E-Space attribution as tentative
E-SPACE CALISTUS.purpose: Five spacecraft launched together on an Electron in August 2025 and catalogued under Rwandan registration, tracked elsewhere as Calistus A to E. They are understood to be demonstration satellites validating the systems for E-Space's proposed very large communications constellation, the Rwandan government having filed an ITU application for up to 300,000 satellites to be operated under Rwandan authority by E-Space. Neither the operator nor the Rwandan authorities have published payload details, so the attribution and the mission should both be treated as inference from the filing rather than declared fact.

E3TESTER.organization: ETRI (Electronics and Telecommunications Research Institute) / Nara Space Technology
E3TESTER.purpose: EEE Tester-1, a 12U Korean cubesat with one job: give domestically made electrical, electronic and electromechanical parts the flight heritage they lack. It carries nine types of Korean-developed components plus memory semiconductors including Samsung DRAM and NAND flash, and reports how they behave under real radiation and thermal cycling. Assembly, integration and test were done by Nara Space Technology, and it flew on Korea’s Nuri launch vehicle.

EAGLEEYE.purpose: EagleEye is the largest satellite built in Poland, a roughly 50 kg microsatellite from a consortium of Creotech Instruments, Scanway and the Space Research Centre of the Polish Academy of Sciences. Its payload is the SOP200, the largest Earth-observation telescope designed and built in Poland - a 200 mm aperture dual-sensor refractor-reflector imaging in the visible and near infrared, specified at about 1 m ground sampling from a 350 km orbit and about 1.75 m from 500 km. The satellite also carries an onboard supercomputer from CBK PAN that handles compression and cloud screening before downlink.

EGYPTSAT A.purpose: The third flight unit of Egypt's EgyptSat remote sensing programme, built jointly by the National Authority for Remote Sensing and Space Sciences with RKK Energiya in Russia, with the imaging payload supplied from Belarus. Its main mission is land observation and disaster monitoring, and the data are distributed by NARSS's ground control station in Cairo.

ELARA 1.purpose: ElaraSat MMS-1, the first flight of a 100 kg modular satellite platform designed and built on the Gold Coast by Gilmour Space Technologies, flown to validate the bus for future missions and to establish Australian sovereign satellite capability. It carries a hyperspectral imager supplied by CSIRO to monitor water quality - sediment concentration, algal blooms and organic content in coastal and inland waters. The bus can host payloads up to 30 kg and is intended eventually to fly on Gilmour's own Eris launch vehicle.

ELEVATION-1 (ALMAGEST).purpose: A demonstration satellite for Almagest Space, which is developing a secure low-orbit data-relay constellation for government and commercial users. Almagest describes its payload as the first E-band communications payload flown - E-band sits far above the Ka and V bands used by current broadband constellations and offers very wide bandwidth for bulk data movement. The spacecraft was manufactured by XDLINX Space Labs with the E-band payload built around components from Filtronic, Flann and IQ Wireless, and delivered within nine months of contract start.

EMISAT.assessedBy: open-source analysts; ISRO publishes only 'electromagnetic spectrum measurement'
EMISAT.purpose: ISRO publishes EMISAT only as a spacecraft built on its Mini Satellite-2 bus and intended for electromagnetic spectrum measurement. A satellite whose stated job is to measure the electromagnetic spectrum from sun-synchronous orbit is in practice an electronic intelligence receiver: it locates and characterises emitters such as air defence and naval radars. No payload description has been published by the operator, so the ELINT role is an assessment drawn from the mission's stated function, not a documented capability.

EOS-4.purpose: EOS-04, a radar imaging satellite designed to provide high quality images under all weather conditions for agriculture, forestry and plantations, soil moisture and hydrology, and flood mapping. It continues India's line of operational radar imagers; soil moisture and flood mapping are precisely the applications that fail with optical sensors during a monsoon, which is why they justify a radar spacecraft.

EOS-8.purpose: An ISRO microsatellite flying three payloads: an electro-optical infrared imager working in mid-wave and long-wave infrared for day and night surveillance, disaster and fire detection; a GNSS-Reflectometry receiver; and a silicon-carbide ultraviolet dosimeter that monitors UV irradiance at the crew module viewport for the Gaganyaan human spaceflight programme. The GNSS-R payload is the METOC-relevant one -- it demonstrates retrieving ocean surface winds, soil moisture, cryosphere state and flood extent from navigation-satellite signals reflected off the surface.

ERMIS3.organization: National and Kapodistrian University of Athens
ERMIS3.purpose: ERMIS-3 is the third of three 8U CubeSats of the ERMIS constellation, system-engineered by the National and Kapodistrian University of Athens under the ESA-funded Greek CubeSat In-Orbit Validation programme and, unlike its two siblings, designed and manufactured by the university itself. The constellation demonstrates a bundle of Greek-developed technologies at once: standards-based satellite IoT and 5G non-terrestrial connectivity, inter-satellite links, FPGA-accelerated hyperspectral image compression at about 5 m ground sampling, and laser optical downlink at up to 1 Gbit/s to the Helmos optical ground station.

EROS C3.purpose: An ImageSat International very-high-resolution imaging satellite built by Israel Aerospace Industries on the OPTSAT-3000 bus, producing panchromatic imagery at 0.30 m and multispectral at 0.60 m. ISI sells the capacity to government customers -- it has publicly announced a five-year contract with an undisclosed strategic customer for 30 cm imaging from EROS C3 and C2 -- which is the commercial-operator route to what is functionally reconnaissance-grade imagery.

ES'HAIL 1.purpose: Qatar's first satellite, a Space Systems/Loral spacecraft at the 25.5 degrees East broadcasting hot spot with both Ku and Ka-band payloads. Es'hailSat operates it for premium direct-to-home television -- beIN Sports and Al Jazeera among its customers -- and for newsgathering, corporate networks, GSM backhaul, IP trunking and government services.

ES'HAIL 2.purpose: Es'hailSat's second Qatari satellite, a Mitsubishi-built Ku and Ka-band spacecraft near 26 degrees East supporting broadcasting, telecommunications and government services with anti-jamming protection and back-up for Es'hail-1. It also carries the first amateur radio transponders ever placed in geostationary orbit -- a joint project of Es'hailSat, the Qatar Amateur Radio Society and AMSAT-DL, designated Qatar-OSCAR 100 -- which gives amateur operators from Brazil to Thailand a permanently available relay instead of a few minutes per low-orbit pass.

ESA ARCTIC WEATHER SATELLITE.purpose: The Arctic Weather Satellite is a small ESA prototype carrying a cross-track microwave sounder — the instrument class that gives numerical weather prediction its temperature and humidity profiles through cloud, where infrared sounders cannot see. The Arctic is the worst-observed region for short-range forecasting because the polar-orbiting sounders that do cover it are few and their revisit is slow, and this mission was built in three years on a tight budget to show that a constellation of cheap copies could fix that. It worked: the follow-on constellation, EPS-Sterna, is now going ahead, and the prototype's data were adopted for operational forecasting before it had finished proving itself.

ESA BIOMASS.purpose: Biomass carries the first P-band synthetic-aperture radar ever flown. The long wavelength — around 70 cm — passes through forest canopy and scatters from trunks and large branches, which is what makes it possible to weigh a forest from orbit rather than infer its mass from the greenness of its top. The same wavelength is why the mission took so long to fly: P-band is shared with defence radars, so Biomass is barred from transmitting over North America and Europe, and its measurements are also strongly affected by the ionosphere, which the mission has to correct for.

ESA CELESTE LEO-PNT.purpose: The first two satellites of ESA's Celeste in-orbit demonstration, launched on 28 March 2026 into a quasi-polar orbit around 510 km to test a low-Earth-orbit navigation layer complementary to Galileo. The case for LEO-PNT is straightforward: a signal from 500 km arrives some thirty decibels stronger than one from 23,000 km and its geometry changes fast, which makes it far harder to jam and far quicker to converge — both of which matter to any user operating where GNSS is being interfered with. Celeste is planned to grow to eleven spacecraft.

ESA CHEOPS.purpose: CHEOPS, the CHaracterising ExOPlanet Satellite, is ESA's first small science mission. It does not search for new planets: it revisits stars already known to host one and measures the tiny dip in brightness as the planet transits, precisely enough to pin down the planet's radius. Combined with a mass from ground-based radial-velocity work, that radius gives a density, and density is what separates a rocky world from a gas envelope.

ESA CLUSTER II.purpose: A Cluster spacecraft: ESA flew four identical satellites in a tetrahedron through the Earth's magnetosphere so that, for the first time, the boundaries the solar wind pushes around could be measured in three dimensions instead of along a single track. Four points let you tell a moving boundary from a changing one — the difference between a magnetopause that is oscillating and a magnetopause that is being compressed — which is the measurement that underlies much of what is now taught about magnetic reconnection and the storm-time magnetosphere. The highly elliptical orbit carries each spacecraft from low altitude out past 130,000 km, cutting the bow shock, magnetopause and tail on every pass.

ESA CRYOSAT-2.purpose: CryoSat-2 carries SIRAL, a radar altimeter built specifically for ice. In synthetic-aperture mode it sharpens the along-track footprint enough to see between floes and measure sea-ice freeboard, and in interferometric mode a second antenna resolves which way a sloping ice-sheet margin is tilted so the return can be placed correctly on the ground. Its orbit is deliberately steep — 92° inclination — to reach further into the polar caps than most Earth-observation satellites. The sea-ice thickness record it produces is one of the primary inputs to Arctic ice forecasting.

ESA CYBERCUBE.purpose: CyberCUBE is an ESA cubesat flown as an in-orbit cybersecurity laboratory: a real satellite, in a real orbit, that security researchers can attack and defend under controlled conditions. Space-system security has until now been studied almost entirely on the ground, where the radio link, the onboard software and the operations timeline can all be simulated but none of them behaves quite as it does in flight. The KA-SAT attack of 2022 is the standing argument for why this testbed exists.

ESA EDRS-C.purpose: EDRS-C is a node of the European Data Relay System, marketed as the SpaceDataHighway: a geostationary satellite that picks up data from low-orbiting spacecraft over a laser link and pushes it to the ground in near real time. Without a relay, a satellite in low Earth orbit can only downlink when it flies over a ground station, so imagery taken over a distant area may wait most of an orbit; a laser relay collapses that delay to minutes. The Copernicus Sentinels are its principal users, and the same architecture is what makes timely satellite imagery of a fast-moving situation possible at all.

ESA ESEO.purpose: ESEO, the European Student Earth Orbiter, is a microsatellite built almost entirely by university students across ESA member states under the agency's education programme, carrying student-developed payloads including a camera, a dosimeter and an amateur-radio transponder. Its purpose is as much the training as the data: the mission exists so that a cohort of engineers has flown hardware before they reach industry.

ESA HYDROGNSS.purpose: A HydroGNSS satellite: an ESA Scout mission that measures the Earth by listening to navigation signals bouncing off it. GNSS reflectometry uses the existing GPS and Galileo transmissions as free illuminators and needs only a receiver, so a small, cheap spacecraft can retrieve soil moisture, inundated wetland, freeze-thaw state and sea-ice extent. The same technique measures ocean surface roughness, which is why reflectometry keeps appearing in proposals for cheap wind and sea-state observation.

ESA PROBA.purpose: A PROBA spacecraft: ESA's small in-orbit technology demonstrators, each of which turned into a working science mission. PROBA-1 flew an autonomous onboard control system and the CHRIS hyperspectral imager and is still returning data decades past its planned life. PROBA-2 carries SWAP, an extreme-ultraviolet imager of the solar corona, and LYRA, a fast ultraviolet radiometer — a small but genuine solar-monitoring asset that this site's own space-weather teaching draws on. PROBA-V carried the Vegetation instrument continuity mission after SPOT-5 retired.

ESA PROBA-3.purpose: PROBA-3 is a pair of spacecraft flying as one instrument: the Occulter Spacecraft holds a 1.4-metre disc precisely between the Sun and the Coronagraph Spacecraft about 150 metres behind it, casting an artificial eclipse so the corona can be observed close to the solar limb without the scattered light that ruins a conventional coronagraph. Holding millimetre-scale relative position at that separation, unaided, for hours at a time is the technology being demonstrated; the science return is a view of the inner corona where the solar wind is accelerated. The highly elliptical orbit gives long, quiet formation-flying arcs near apogee.

ESA SENTINEL-6 MICHAEL FREILICH.purpose: Sentinel-6 Michael Freilich is the reference ocean altimeter: the satellite that continues, without a break, the sea-surface height record begun by TOPEX/Poseidon in 1992 and carried by the Jason series since. It flies the same 1,336 km, 66°-inclination repeat orbit those missions used, because a climate-quality sea-level record depends on measuring the same ground track at the same times for decades. The data are operational as well as scientific — altimetric sea-surface height drives the mesoscale eddy and current analyses used for ocean forecasting and for acoustic prediction — and the mission is run jointly by ESA, EUMETSAT, NASA and NOAA.

ESA SMILE.organization: European Space Agency / Chinese Academy of Sciences
ESA SMILE.purpose: SMILE — Solar wind Magnetosphere Ionosphere Link Explorer — is a joint ESA and Chinese Academy of Sciences mission that does something no earlier spacecraft could: it images the magnetosphere's boundary directly. Solar-wind ions exchanging charge with neutral atoms near the magnetopause emit soft X-rays, and SMILE's Soft X-ray Imager photographs that emission from far out on a highly elliptical orbit while an ultraviolet imager watches the northern aurora at the same time. In place of the single-point measurements every earlier mission returned, that gives a picture of how the whole boundary responds to a gust of solar wind.

ESA SMOS.purpose: SMOS — Soil Moisture and Ocean Salinity — carries MIRAS, an L-band interferometric radiometer with sixty-nine small receivers on three deployed arms that synthesise an aperture no single dish could carry to orbit. At L-band the ocean's brightness temperature responds to salinity and the land's to soil moisture, so one instrument returns two variables that drive the water cycle. For a METOC user the salinity fields matter because they set near-surface density and stratification, and the same radiometer has proved able to measure very high wind speeds through rain, where scatterometers saturate.

ESA SWARM CONSTELLATION.purpose: A Swarm satellite: three spacecraft that map the Earth's magnetic field and its sources — core, crust, oceans, ionosphere and magnetosphere — with vector magnetometers on a rigid optical bench. The formation is the instrument: Swarm A and C fly side by side at the lower altitude so the pair can separate a spatial gradient from a time variation, while Swarm B flies higher and drifts in local time. The mission also measures the ionospheric plasma the spacecraft passes through, which is why it turns up in space-weather work as well as in geomagnetism — the field model it produces is what a magnetic compass, a directional drilling rig and an ionospheric correction all quietly depend on.

ETIHAD-SAT.purpose: The Mohammed Bin Rashid Space Centre's first synthetic aperture radar satellite, developed in partnership with South Korea's Satrec Initiative. MBRSC's stated reason for adding it is that radar returns high-resolution images in all weather conditions -- through cloud, dust and at night -- which the centre's optical satellites KhalifaSat and MBZ-SAT cannot do. For a Gulf operator that means usable imagery during the shamal season and after dark.

ETV-A1 (SEN).purpose: The first satellite of Sen's planned ETV constellation of ultra-high-definition video spacecraft, a 16U CubeSat built by NanoAvionics. It carries four cameras at different spatial scales, from whole continents and oceans down to about 1.5 m ground resolution, and streams recorded and live UHD - including 8K from the sharpest camera.
