SUPERBIRD 8 DSN-1.purpose: DSN-1/Superbird-8, a dual-purpose spacecraft built by Mitsubishi Electric on its DS2000 platform. The Superbird-8 side carries Ku- and Ka-band capacity for SKY Perfect JSAT's commercial services in Japan, replacing the 18-year-old Superbird-B2 at 162 degrees East; riding with it is the X-band DSN-1 payload for Japan's Ministry of Defense. One spacecraft therefore carries both commercial capacity and an element of Japan's dedicated military X-band SATCOM.

SWEDEN MATS.organization: Swedish National Space Agency / Stockholm University
SWEDEN MATS.purpose: MATS — Mesospheric Airglow/Aerosol Tomography and Spectroscopy — is a Swedish research satellite that images the faint airglow and noctilucent clouds at the edge of space in limb view, and reconstructs them tomographically in three dimensions. The target is atmospheric gravity waves: disturbances that carry energy and momentum upward from weather in the lower atmosphere into the mesosphere and thermosphere, where they influence the density that low-orbiting satellites fly through. It is one of the few missions measuring that coupling directly.

SWISSCUBE.purpose: SwissCube is a 1U cubesat built by students at EPFL and launched in 2009, carrying a small telescope to photograph the nightglow — the faint oxygen emission at around 762 nm in the upper atmosphere, whose brightness varies with the state of the thermosphere. It was Switzerland's first entirely home-built satellite and it has operated far beyond its planned life. Its name is also a standing example of a name-matching trap: SWISSCUBE contains the letters ISS and has nothing whatever to do with the space station.

Sateliot.purpose: A Sateliot nanosatellite: the Barcelona operator is building a low-orbit constellation that implements the 3GPP 5G NB-IoT non-terrestrial-network standard directly, so that unmodified commercial IoT devices - and, in the direct-to-device case, ordinary handsets - can connect through the satellite as if it were another cell of their mobile operator's network. The four spacecraft catalogued here flew as the 'Revolution' mission that took the company into commercial service. Sateliot markets the capability to governments as well as industry, naming critical-infrastructure monitoring, border surveillance, crisis response and tactical communications alongside its logistics and agriculture business.

SaudiGeoSat 1 / Hellas Sat 4.purpose: A single Lockheed Martin LM2100 spacecraft carrying two national payloads at 39 degrees East. The SaudiGeoSat 1 side provides Ka-band spot-beam services for Saudi Arabia's King Abdulaziz City for Science and Technology; the Hellas Sat 4 side provides Ku-band regional beams for Hellas Sat, the Arabsat subsidiary, covering Europe, the Middle East and southern Africa. Shared-bus arrangements like this are how mid-sized national operators buy geostationary capacity without funding a whole satellite each.

Startical IOD.purpose: A Startical in-orbit demonstrator: Startical is the joint venture of ENAIRE, Spain's air navigation service provider, and Indra, prototyping a constellation of over 200 low-orbit satellites that would carry VHF voice and datalink between pilots and air traffic controllers, plus aircraft surveillance, from space. IOD-1 made the first VHF voice call between a pilot and a controller through a satellite to international aviation standards, and IOD-2 extended the test campaign under the EU-funded ECHOES project. The problem it addresses is the one every oceanic controller knows: beyond about 350 km from the coast aircraft drop off ground radar and fall back on high-latency HF, which forces larger separation minima.

T.MICROSAT BELLBIRD.purpose: T.MicroSat, also called Bellbird, an 8U CubeSat developed by Tron Future under Taiwan Space Agency supervision as part of TASA's startup support programme. The mission is to demonstrate high-speed broadband and inter-satellite links in orbit, a step toward Taiwanese-built low-orbit communications — the capability Taiwan is pursuing because its undersea cables are a single point of failure in a crisis.

T2V.purpose: THEOS-2, the very-high-resolution element of the second generation of Thailand's GISTDA Earth observation system and the successor to THEOS-1. Built by Airbus, it delivers 0.5 m ground resolution imagery, and the contract deliberately included a capacity-building programme under which Thai engineers assembled and tested the companion small satellite in-country and were trained on the integrated geo-information and ground segment. GISTDA distributes the imagery for natural resource, coastal, maritime traffic and pollution monitoring.

TDS 1 (TECHDEMOSAT-1).purpose: TechDemoSat-1, SSTL's UK payload demonstration mission, whose most consequential passenger for a METOC audience is the SGR-ReSI GNSS-reflectometry instrument. It collects GPS signals after they have bounced off the sea surface and processes them into delay-Doppler maps, from which ocean roughness and surface wind speed are retrieved - scatterometry without needing a transmitter, from a low-mass low-power receiver. Published results showed wind speed retrieved against ASCAT with about 2.2 m/s precision between 3 and 18 m/s, and the same reflections carry information about sea ice, snow depth and soil moisture.

TECHSAT 1B.purpose: TechSat/Gurwin-II, a microsatellite built by students of the Technion in Haifa with industrial and government support, and part of the Asher Space Research Institute's TechSat family. It is also known to radio operators as OSCAR-32. Its purpose was to develop and fly space-qualified systems designed at a university, and it went on to operate successfully in orbit for many years -- an unusually long life for a student spacecraft of its era.

TELEOS 2.purpose: Singapore's first synthetic aperture radar satellite, developed by ST Engineering with the Defence Science and Technology Agency on behalf of the Singapore government and flying a Singapore-built polarimetric SAR payload. It delivers 1 m imagery in all weather, day or night, and because it sits in a near-equatorial orbit at 10 degrees inclination it makes an average of fourteen passes a day over the equatorial belt. That combination of full polarimetry, all-weather imaging and very high revisit over the region's shipping lanes is a serious maritime domain awareness asset for the Malacca and Singapore Straits.

TELESAT LEO 3.purpose: Telesat's low-orbit demonstrator, a 30 kg microsatellite built by Toronto's Space Flight Laboratory on the DEFIANT bus and carrying Ka- and V-band payloads. It exists to keep customer and vendor testing alive after the Phase 1 LEO prototype was decommissioned, and it operates under an existing ITU filing for Telesat Lightspeed, the company's planned enterprise-class broadband constellation. It is a pathfinder for antenna and modem development, not an operational service satellite.

TELKOM 3S.purpose: A Thales Alenia Space Spacebus-4000B2 satellite built for PT Telekomunikasi Indonesia to replace Telkom-3, which was stranded in an unusable orbit by a launch failure in 2012. From 118 degrees East it increases Telkom's C-band capacity and adds Ku-band for high-definition television and remote GSM and internet backhaul. Telkom is the state-controlled incumbent carrier, so this is national telecoms infrastructure rather than a broadcast-only asset.

TELKOM-4.purpose: Telkom-4, named Merah Putih after the Indonesian flag, is an SSL-1300 geostationary communications satellite operated by PT Telekomunikasi Indonesia from 108 degrees East with a sixteen-year design life. It replaced the ageing Telkom-1 capacity and carries C-band coverage reaching beyond Indonesia into South and South East Asia. Telkom operates the largest domestic fleet in Indonesia and this is its principal wide-beam workhorse.

TELKOMSAT 113BT.purpose: Merah Putih-2, formerly designated Telkomsat HTS 113BT, a Thales Alenia Space Spacebus-4000B2 high-throughput satellite launched in February 2024 for Telkom's subsidiary Telkomsat. It delivers more than 32 Gbps in C and Ku-band across the whole Indonesian archipelago and was bought specifically to strengthen connectivity infrastructure and narrow the digital divide between Java and the outer islands.

TELSTAR (TELESAT).purpose: Telesat's international Telstar satellites, the export arm of the Canadian operator's geostationary business, as distinct from the domestic Anik and Nimiq craft. The Vantage generation combines broad regional beams with high-throughput spot beams: Telstar 19 Vantage carries Ka-band spots over the North Atlantic and Caribbean for mobility users plus Ku-band beams over Brazil and the Andean region, and Ka-band high-throughput coverage of northern Canada. For a maritime operator that translates directly into contracted broadband over ocean transit routes rather than only over land.

TERRASAR-X TANDEM-X.purpose: TerraSAR-X and TanDEM-X are two nearly identical German X-band radar satellites flown by DLR with Airbus under a public-private partnership. Their notable achievement is what they did together: for several years they flew in a close helix formation, a few hundred metres apart, acting as a single bistatic interferometer, and from that produced WorldDEM — a globally consistent elevation model far better than anything available before. Individually each is a capable operational radar, running modes from 25 cm staring spotlight for image intelligence out to a 270 km wide ScanSAR swath that ESA describes as particularly suitable for maritime applications. Note the registry writes the first of them as TERRA SAR X with spaces, which is not the same string as the NASA satellite TERRA.

THAICOM.purpose: Two of the geostationary satellites of Thaicom, the Thai operator whose fleet reaches roughly two-thirds of the world's population from the 78.5 degrees East neighbourhood. Thaicom 6 and Thaicom 8 carry C and Ku-band video, broadcast and data services over Asia, Africa and Oceania, and the operator's business is split between broadcasters expanding into new markets, telecom operators buying rural broadband backhaul and government administrations extending national communications. For the Indian Ocean region Thaicom is one of the principal non-Western commercial capacity suppliers.

THE ARAB SATELLITE 813.organization: Arab Space Cooperation Group / UAEU NSSTC
THE ARAB SATELLITE 813.purpose: The first Arab space project led by the UAE and built collaboratively by the Arab Space Cooperation Group, an eleven-country grouping formed in 2019; the spacecraft was developed at the National Space Science and Technology Center of United Arab Emirates University. It is the first satellite in the UAE to carry hyperspectral imaging, with 205 spectral bands for environmental and climatic study and detailed surface observation. Its second purpose is explicitly capability-building -- training Arab engineers in assembling and testing microsatellites.

THEOS.purpose: The Thailand Earth Observation System satellite, also called Thaichote, funded by the Thai science ministry, built by EADS Astrium and operated by GISTDA, Thailand's national space agency. It was bought to give Thailand affordable sovereign access to space imagery and, just as importantly, to establish the ground infrastructure and trained staff for a continuing national space programme. It combines a 2 m panchromatic channel with a wide-swath multispectral imager for mapping, agriculture and disaster work.

THOR.purpose: A Thor geostationary satellite operated by Telenor Satellite of Norway, carrying Ku-band direct-to-home television across the Nordic and central European market from 1° West, and — in the case of Thor 7 — a high-throughput Ka-band maritime payload aimed squarely at shipping in the North Sea, the Norwegian Sea, the Baltic and the Mediterranean. Thor 7's maritime capacity is a good illustration of where commercial broadband at sea actually comes from: a spot-beam payload sized for the sea lanes rather than the land mass.

THURAYA.purpose: A geostationary L-band mobile satellite system operated from the UAE, serving energy, enterprise, government, maritime and leisure users on the move -- the beyond-line-of-sight voice and IP service that works from a handheld or vehicle terminal where there is no cellular coverage. The operator describes the current spacecraft, Thuraya-4, as a sovereign L-band satellite delivering jam-proof, secure connectivity across Europe, the Middle East and North Africa, Central Asia and Africa, built for governments, fleets and aviation.

TIBA-1.purpose: A geostationary communications satellite for the Government of Egypt, with the communications payload built by Thales Alenia Space and an Airbus Eurostar E3000 platform. The payload is dual-mission in Ka-band, covering secure government communications as well as broadband -- a national SATCOM asset rather than a commercial leasing platform.

TIGER (OQ TECHNOLOGY).purpose: Two 6U satellites of the TIGER constellation flown by OQ Technology, a Luxembourg-based operator that registers part of its fleet through Rwanda. They carry narrowband 5G non-terrestrial-network IoT payloads, effectively acting as orbiting cell towers so that standard NB-IoT devices can report from places with no ground network. TIGER-7 and TIGER-8 were built by NanoAvionics and completed the operator's first batch of ten satellites, the point at which it claimed global narrowband IoT coverage.

TIGRISAT.organization: Sapienza University of Rome / Iraqi Ministry of Higher Education
TIGRISAT.purpose: TigriSat is Iraq's first satellite: a 3U cubesat built by Iraqi students at Sapienza University of Rome, carrying a colour camera tasked with detecting the dust storms that regularly close airspace and ports across Iraq. It is a student mission and an education programme, and it is also a reasonable choice of first payload — dust is the atmospheric hazard that most affects the country.

TIRSAT.purpose: TIRSAT, a 3U thermal-infrared CubeSat operated by Japan Space Systems, with the satellite bus and operations by Seiren, the sensor by Vision Sensing and ground operations by ArkEdge Space. It senses heat sources such as factories in the thermal infrared and infers from them whether a facility is running - it was built under a Japanese government programme on using satellites to read the state of industrial supply chains - and it also demonstrated a lightweight 3U deployment mechanism in orbit.

TISAT 1.organization: SUPSI (University of Applied Sciences of Southern Switzerland)
TISAT 1.purpose: TIsat-1 is a 1U cubesat built by students at SUPSI in Ticino, Switzerland, flown to test how commercial-grade electronics, wiring and coatings actually survive the low-Earth-orbit environment — thermal cycling, atomic oxygen and radiation — over years rather than months. It has long outlived its design life, which is itself the result the mission was after.

TKSAT 1.purpose: Tupac Katari 1, Bolivia's first and only communications satellite, operated by the Agencia Boliviana Espacial and delivered in orbit by China Great Wall Industry Corporation on a DFH-4 bus. The agency describes it as working in C, Ku FSS, Ku BSS and Ka bands to carry voice, data and video, with internet access and satellite television being the services most in demand from users spread across Bolivian national territory. It is the standard Chinese in-orbit-delivery package: satellite, launch, ground stations and operator training bought as one contract.

TPA-1.purpose: A 3U CubeSat from Te Punaha Atea, the University of Auckland's Space Institute, built on a NanoAvionics platform as New Zealand's first university-led end-to-end mission - concept, build, delivery and operations in house. It carries institute-developed payloads including an Earth observation and deployables imager, a thermal monitoring payload, a deployable inspection boom, and a miniaturised dragsail for end-of-life disposal. It is explicitly a capability-building first step in a planned series of application-led missions.

TRITON 1.purpose: A 3U CubeSat built by ISIS of Delft as a test bed for an experimental receiver designed to pick up Automatic Identification System messages from ships - an early attempt to shrink space-based maritime traffic monitoring to nanosatellite scale. The plan after launch was to characterise the AIS receiver in orbit for about three months and then activate a single-channel FM-to-DSB amateur transponder for the radio community.

TRITON FORMOSAT-7R.purpose: Triton, Taiwan's first domestically manufactured meteorological satellite. It carries a GNSS-Reflectometry receiver: instead of imaging, it listens to navigation-satellite signals bouncing off the sea surface and reads the roughness of that reflection, which yields ocean surface wind speed. That is a direct METOC product — wind over open water where there are no buoys — and it feeds typhoon forecasting, the reason Taiwan built it.

TROLL.purpose: TROLL is a 6U CubeSat from the Brno company TRL Space, the largest Czech commercial satellite, carrying a hyperspectral camera and a data-processing unit that reduces the imagery on board before it is downlinked in S-band. It is a working commercial mission rather than a demonstrator: the Czech Environmental Inspectorate, part of the environment ministry, uses its data operationally, for example to find illegal landfills and waste dumps hidden in forest.

TSAT-1A.purpose: A sub-metre optical imaging satellite assembled in India by Tata Advanced Systems at its Vemagal plant in Karnataka, under a technology-transfer partnership with Satellogic. The companies present it as the first sub-metre resolution optical satellite built in India, and it marks the point at which Indian private industry began delivering complete imaging spacecraft rather than components into someone else's programme.

TU BERLIN SMALL SATELLITES.purpose: A small satellite of the Technische Universität Berlin space technology group, which has been flying student- and research-built spacecraft since the TUBSAT series of the 1990s and is one of the longest-running university programmes of its kind. The individual missions differ — BEESAT proved that a picosatellite could carry usable reaction wheels, TechnoSat flew a set of new component technologies, and SALSAT carried a spectrum analyser that produced the first open-access map of radio-frequency use as seen from orbit, addressing the growing interference problem in a crowded spectrum.

TURKMENALEM MONACOSAT.organization: Turkmenistan National Space Agency / Space Systems International-Monaco
TURKMENALEM MONACOSAT.purpose: TürkmenÄlem 52°E / MonacoSAT is Turkmenistan's first satellite, launched in 2015 into a slot whose orbital filing belongs to Monaco: the spacecraft carries Ku-band capacity for Turkmen national television and telecommunications, and Space Systems International-Monaco holds a share of the transponders in exchange for the frequency rights. It is a clean example of how a state with no orbital filings of its own gets to geostationary orbit — you buy access to somebody else's registration.

TURKSAT 5B.purpose: Turksat's high-throughput Ka-band satellite at 42 degrees East. Turksat states it carries more than 55 Gbps of data transmission capacity in the Ka band, covering large parts of the Middle East and Africa, and that it also guarantees redundancy for the Turksat 3A and 4A satellites. Turksat markets it explicitly for uninterrupted communication beyond land borders in every sector from maritime to aviation, which makes it one of the larger commercial Ka pools available to ships transiting the eastern Mediterranean, Red Sea and Gulf.

TURKSAT 6A.purpose: Turkiye's first domestically designed and built communications satellite, and a genuine national first: Turksat describes it as the country's first indigenous and national communications satellite, developed by TUBITAK UZAY with TUSAS, ASELSAN and CTECH and commissioned in 2025 after launch in July 2024. It operates at 42 degrees East in Ku, Ka and Q/V bands, and Turksat says its coverage extends the fleet's reach eastward as far as India, Thailand, Malaysia and Indonesia. Its significance is industrial as much as operational, since it moved Turkiye into the small group of states that can build their own GEO comsat.

TURKSAT GEO FLEET.purpose: Part of the geostationary fleet of Turksat, the Turkish state-owned satellite operator that carries broadcasting, broadband and government traffic from the 31 degrees East and 42 degrees East orbital slots. Turksat 3A and 4A work the 42 degrees East position with Turkiye, western and eastern beams; Turksat 4B adds C-band Africa and Ka high-throughput coverage; Turksat 5A holds 31 degrees East with beams reaching West Africa, MENA, Germany and South Africa. For a maritime or expeditionary planner the practical point is that this fleet is the dominant commercial Ku-band supply over Turkiye, the Black Sea approaches, the Levant and much of North and West Africa.

TYCHE (UK SPACE COMMAND).organization: UK Ministry of Defence / UK Space Command
TYCHE (UK SPACE COMMAND).purpose: The first satellite fully owned by the UK Ministry of Defence and UK Space Command's first spacecraft able to capture daytime imagery and video of the Earth's surface. It was procured for £22 million from Surrey Satellite Technology Ltd by Defence Equipment and Support, and it is the first launch under the MoD's space-based ISR programme, which is intended to field a constellation and its ground segment by 2031. The MoD frames it as an intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance capability that will also support disaster monitoring and mapping; it is a demonstrator of a national capability rather than an operational constellation in itself.

TYVAK-182A (ELO Alpha).purpose: Catalogued as TYVAK-182A, this spacecraft is ELO Alpha - Eutelsat LEO for Objects - a 6U CubeSat built and operated by Tyvak International in Turin as the prototype for a Eutelsat low-orbit Internet-of-Things constellation. It collects short narrowband messages from ground devices using the same omnidirectional antennas as terrestrial IoT networks, drawing on Sigfox technology, and dumps them daily to a ground station on Svalbard. The point of the mission is to measure how well a LEO satellite can backhaul data from assets outside terrestrial coverage.

UHETSAT (microHETSat).purpose: Catalogued as UHETSAT, this is microHETSat, a sub-75 kg SITAEL microsatellite flown with ESA and ASI purely to qualify a low-power Hall-effect electric propulsion system in orbit. The propulsion subsystem - SITAEL's 100 W-class HT100 thruster with its own hollow cathodes, xenon tank and fluidic system - is the mission: the declared goals are at least 1000 ignition cycles, at least 250 cumulative hours of firing and a single burn longer than 600 seconds. Electric propulsion at this power level is what lets small Earth-observation satellites hold very low orbits and phase constellations without a chemical stage.

UKUBE 1.purpose: The UK Space Agency's first CubeSat, built by Clyde Space in Glasgow as the pilot for a national CubeSat programme and the first Scottish-built satellite. It carried six UK payloads, among them TOPCAT, a dual-frequency GPS receiver from the University of Bath described by the agency as the first GPS device aimed at measuring plasmaspheric space weather - it images the electron density of the topside ionosphere and plasmasphere by tomography, the region that dominates GNSS signal delay. Other payloads tested radiation effects on hardware and the use of cosmic radiation to improve communications-satellite security.

UM5.purpose: A UM5 nanosatellite: Morocco's first university-built spacecraft, developed at the Centre for Research in Space Technologies of the Mohammadia School of Engineers at Mohammed V University in Rabat, with the national research centre CNRST and the Royal Centre for Space Studies and Research. UM5-EOSat carries an Earth-observation payload and UM5-Ribat a technology and communications demonstration; the pair are a national capability-building exercise as much as a data mission.

UNICORN.purpose: A Unicorn-2 PocketQube: Alba Orbital of Glasgow developed this 3p platform with ESA to get roughly 3U cubesat capability into a satellite an eighth the size, cutting hardware and launch cost by more than half. The company's own application for it is night-time Earth imagery — mapping power outages and lit activity after dark — and the platform is also sold to other operators as a way to fly a small payload cheaply.

UNIFORM 1.purpose: The first satellite of the UNIFORM project, a Japanese university-led programme whose entire purpose is detecting wildfires and getting the fire information to the people fighting them as close to real time as possible. Its primary payload is a thermal infrared sensor sized and priced for a microsatellite, roughly 200 m ground sampling over a 100 km swath, with a visible camera to help confirm the detection. The project deliberately covers the ground station network and data delivery as well as the spacecraft.

UNISAT.purpose: A UniSat microsatellite from GAUSS Srl, the Rome company grown out of the Sapienza aerospace school's GAUSS laboratory. The UniSat spacecraft are dual-purpose: they act as in-orbit deployers, carrying CubeSats and PocketQubes up and releasing them once on station, and as flexible in-orbit demonstrators for customers' hardware and for GAUSS's own work on attitude control, optics, RF and space-debris detection. UniSat-7 added an octagonal three-axis-stabilised bus, nadir and wide-angle cameras and an experimental REGULUS nano-propulsion system, and keeps an open amateur-radio telemetry downlink.

UOSAT 2 / OSCAR 11.purpose: The second satellite built by the University of Surrey team that went on to found SSTL, taken from inception to launch in five months in 1984. It was the first amateur satellite to carry a digital communications package into orbit and the first controlled by a processor running software written in Forth, and it flew a magnetometer, a CCD camera, a Geiger-Muller tube and a microphone for micrometeoroid impacts alongside a speech synthesiser. Its 145.826 MHz beacon has been heard transmitting telemetry more than forty years after launch, which makes it one of the longest-lived working spacecraft in this catalog.

UVSQ-SAT NG.purpose: UVSQ-Sat NG is a French research cubesat from the LATMOS atmospheric laboratory, continuing the Earth Radiation Budget measurements begun by UVSQ-Sat and Inspire-Sat. The Earth radiation budget — how much solar energy comes in against how much is reflected and radiated away — is the single number that determines whether the planet is gaining or losing heat, and it has always been measured by a very small number of large instruments. Showing that a cubesat can contribute a broadband measurement to that record is the point of the mission; it also carries a greenhouse-gas spectrometer.

UWE.purpose: A UWE (University of Würzburg Experimental) satellite: a long-running series of 1U cubesats, each of which qualifies one subsystem needed for cooperating formations of very small spacecraft. UWE-3 flew a miniature attitude determination and control system, UWE-4 an electric propulsion system small enough for a 1U — the first of its kind to demonstrate orbit control on that scale. The series is deliberately incremental, and the NetSat formation mission is where the pieces were put together.

VELOX C1.purpose: VELOX-CI, a 123 kg NTU microsatellite placed in a near-equatorial orbit specifically to get a high revisit rate over the tropics. Its payload is a 3D atmospheric measurement package built around a GPS radio occultation module and a radio frequency probe: by tracking GNSS signals as they are bent by the atmosphere on the limb, it recovers upper-atmosphere temperature, humidity and pressure profiles. Radio occultation soundings of this kind are assimilated into numerical weather prediction, and tropical profiles are the ones global models are thinnest on.

VERTECS.purpose: VERTECS, a 6U astronomical nanosatellite led by the Kyushu Institute of Technology with JAXA and several Japanese universities. It observes the visible extragalactic background light — the faint diffuse glow left by all the stars that have ever formed — to constrain star formation history, a measurement that is very hard from the ground because airglow and zodiacal light swamp it.

VINASAT.purpose: Vietnam's two geostationary communications satellites, both Lockheed Martin A2100 spacecraft procured turnkey by Vietnam Posts and Telecommunications Group; VINASAT-1 in 2008 was the first satellite system Vietnam ever bought. VINASAT-1 carries twelve Ku-band transponders covering Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia, Thailand and part of Myanmar plus C-band transponders reaching across South East Asia to India and Japan, with VINASAT-2 added in 2012 to expand Ku capacity. They underpin national telephony, broadcasting and connectivity to the offshore islands.

VIREON (AAC CLYDE SPACE).purpose: The first two satellites of AAC Clyde Space's VIREON Earth observation constellation, built in Glasgow and backed by UK Space Agency funding through ESA's Pioneer programme. VIREON is deliberately balanced rather than extreme - enough resolution, coverage and revisit frequency to monitor land and vegetation operationally and at scale, paired with data processing, for agriculture, forestry and environmental management. It is the operational follow-on to the company's xSPANCION constellation-production project.

VNREDSAT 1.purpose: The Vietnam Natural Resources, Environment and Disaster-monitoring Satellite, Vietnam's first optical Earth observation spacecraft, built by Astrium and operated by the Space Technology Institute of the Vietnam Academy of Science and Technology with funding from the science ministry. It flies panchromatic and multispectral imagers and was bought to give Vietnam its own imagery for land cover, resource management and disaster response instead of relying on foreign tasking. It remains in extended operations well past its design life.

VRSS.purpose: A Venezuelan Remote Sensing Satellite: VRSS-1 (Miranda) and VRSS-2 (Sucre), both built by the China Academy of Space Technology and launched from Jiuquan under contracts with China Great Wall Industry Corporation, with in-orbit delivery and training of Venezuelan operators as part of the deal. They are Venezuela's second and third spacecraft and its two Earth-observation assets, operated by the national space agency ABAE to supply imagery for urban and agricultural planning and other government decision-making. VRSS-2 carries a 1 m panchromatic and 4 m multispectral imager plus 30 m shortwave and 60 m longwave infrared channels.

WARATAH SEED-1.purpose: A 6U CubeSat run as a pilot space-qualification mission: initiated and part-funded by Investment NSW, it exists to give first-generation payloads from New South Wales startups and research institutions a flight opportunity they could not otherwise afford. It carries technology from three universities and five small companies selected competitively, and it was built by the same University of Sydney CUAVA team as CUAVA-2, deliberately flying overlapping payloads so that a failure on either spacecraft would not cost the programme its results.

WESTPAC.organization: Electro Optic Systems / Western Pacific Laser Tracking Network
WESTPAC.purpose: A passive geodetic sphere with no electronics at all: WESTPAC exists solely to be a laser-ranging target, built by Electro Optic Systems of Australia with the Russian Space Agency for the Western Pacific Laser Tracking Network. Its recessed Fizeau-design retroreflectors are arranged so that on average only about 0.7 corner cubes return any given shot, which removes the array-spread error that limits ordinary laser-ranging spheres and pins the centre-of-mass correction to within half a millimetre. It is optimised for 1.54 micron ranging, eye-safe at any power.

WISDOM-A.purpose: WISDOM-A is one half of an ESA NAVISP demonstration of autonomous satellite collision avoidance: a 6U CubeSat that separates in orbit into two 3U spacecraft, each carrying GNSS and the OWL (Orbital Whereabout Locator) system for positioning, tracking and inter-satellite communication. The pair exchange position data over links of up to 4000 km and then manoeuvre in coordination - one carries mini-thrusters, the other a plasma brake - to demonstrate that satellites can resolve a conjunction between themselves without a human in the loop.

WNISAT.purpose: A WNISAT microsatellite built by Axelspace for Weathernews, the Japanese private weather company, and flown for its own forecasting business rather than for a space agency. The optical cameras observe sea-ice extent, tropical cyclones and volcanic ash clouds, including stereo observation to get cloud and ash-plume height, and WNISAT-1R adds a GNSS-reflectometry receiver that reads sea and land surface conditions from reflected navigation signals in any light or weather. The driving customer requirement is Arctic sea-ice information for ships routing along the Northern Sea Route.

WREN-1.purpose: WREN-1 - Water Resources in Efficient Networks - is a 6U CubeSat developed and operated by the Hungarian company C3S Electronics Development, the largest Hungarian satellite at the time of launch. Its purpose is drought monitoring: it demonstrates a real-time decision-support system built on hyperspectral Earth-observation data, fusing satellite observations with ground measurements and models to raise the spatial and temporal resolution of existing drought monitoring, in support of climate-change adaptation and drought-damage prevention. The satellite manages and prioritises its data on board before transmitting to the ground.

WUERZBURG SONATE-2.purpose: SONATE-2 is a Würzburg nanosatellite flown to test artificial intelligence running on the spacecraft itself. It carries cameras and a processor trained in orbit to recognise features and anomalies, so that the satellite can decide what is worth downlinking instead of sending everything home. Downlink, not sensing, is the binding constraint on most small Earth-observation missions, which is why onboard autonomy of this kind keeps being tried.

XRISM OBSERVATORY.purpose: The X-Ray Imaging and Spectroscopy Mission, a JAXA and NASA observatory with ESA participation. It carries Resolve, an X-ray microcalorimeter that resolves individual spectral lines from hot cosmic plasma at a precision no dispersive instrument can reach for extended sources, and Xtend, a wide-field CCD imager. The mission recovers the science lost when Hitomi failed in 2016.

XSAT.purpose: Singapore's first locally built satellite, a 105 kg microsatellite developed by Nanyang Technological University's Centre for Research in Satellite Technologies with NUS's remote sensing centre and overseas partners including Satrec Initiative, ISRO and DLR. The stated objectives were to develop a low-cost microsatellite bus capable of near-real-time remote sensing, to build national skills and facilities in satellite engineering and to seed university research in the field. It is a capability-building mission rather than an operational imaging asset.

YAHSAT.purpose: The UAE's two-satellite Yahsat system, serving government and commercial users across the Middle East, Africa, Europe and south-west Asia. Yahsat 1B carries both military and civil Ka-band capacity plus a C-band payload and its principal customer is the United Arab Emirates armed forces; Yahsat 1A adds a Ku-band payload. The system's Ka-band military frequencies were certified in 2013 for use with US Wideband Global Satcom terminals, so a WGS-equipped unit can work over the Yahsat footprint -- a relevant detail for coalition operations in the region.

ZACUBE.organization: Cape Peninsula University of Technology / SANSA
ZACUBE.purpose: ZACube-1, also called TshepisoSat, was the first CubeSat built in Africa, produced at the Cape Peninsula University of Technology under the F'SATI programme. Its primary payload is a high-frequency beacon transmitter used to characterise the Earth's ionosphere and, specifically, to calibrate the South African National Space Agency's auroral radar at the SANAE IV base in Antarctica. That is a space-weather instrument with a direct bearing on HF propagation prediction in the southern high latitudes.
